blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Fault diagnosis in power management systems running multiple loads relies on experts manually inspecting current and voltage waveforms, which fails to scale across deployed units. We present TRACK, which pairs a time series encoder with a Small Language Model to produce structured, physics-grounded diagnostic reports, calling tools for exact, verifiable calculations. It operates on-device, keeping proprietary sensor data local and avoiding expensive API calls. We introduce a rubric-based framework that evaluates these reports by scoring structure, signal fidelity, physics reasoning, diagnosis, and actionability through per-criterion verdicts. On a 15-class multi-load simulated benchmark, TRACK achieves over 95% fault-category accuracy and generalizes to out-of-distribution faults, whereas the best encoder-probing baseline reaches only 58% accuracy.
blocks.zh: 运行多负荷的电力管理系统的故障诊断依赖于专家手动检查电流和电压波形,这些波形未能在所部署的单位之间扩大. 我们提出TRACK,它将一个时间序列编码器与一个"小语言"模型相配,以产生结构化的,基于物理的诊断报告,呼吁使用精确,可核查的计算工具. 它在设备上运行,将专有传感器数据保存在本地并避免昂贵的API呼叫. 我们提出一个基于标题的框架,通过评分结构、信号忠贞性、物理推理、诊断和可操作性来评价这些报告。 在一个15级多负荷模拟基准上,TRACK实现了95%以上的断层分类精确度,并概括到分配外断层,而最佳编码-测试基准仅达到58%的精确度.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Modern power management systems supply and protect multiple independent loads (components that consume electrical energy and convert it into work) through central or zonal power management units that continuously senses voltage and current across each channel. From electric vehicles to industrial robotics and grid infrastructure, nearly every electromechanical system depends on power management, and a single undiagnosed fault can halt the entire system. When faults occur, such as an LED failure, connector degradation, or fan stall, diagnostic signatures emerge in the sensed waveforms. Interpreting these signatures requires applying circuit-level physics (e.g., Ohm’s law, power dissipation) and reasoning across multiple channels to isolate the root cause. In practice, this diagnosis is often performed manually by domain experts, a time-intensive and costly process that fails to scale across large deployments.

blocks.en: The challenge is fourfold. First, the model must combine multivariate time series data with varying baseline values (reference measurements under normal operation) and run on-device under memory and compute constraints, so a SLM is required. Second, the generated reasoning must contain a series of correct numerical calculations (e.g., current and voltage analysis), a traditionally difficult task for SLMs because of their fragile numerical representations Bhattacharya et al. (2025) . Third, the model must reason over deviation patterns and explain them, especially for out-of-distribution (OOD) faults. Finally, evaluating the quality of physics reasoning requires domain-specific criteria that standard Natural Language Processing (NLP) metrics, which rely on text overlap, fail to capture.

blocks.en: 2.1 Time Series Data
blocks.zh: 2.1 时间序列数据

blocks.en:
Existing time series reasoning datasets cover financial, weather, and physiological signals Langer et al. (2026) ; Yu et al. (2026) , which differ from electrical circuit waveforms, and focus on classification, MCQ, or captioning. Fault diagnosis in
power management systems, however, requires data that tests generalization to
unseen faults and varying loads. Thus, we introduce a new time series dataset, called Power Management Bench , that is built around a simulated central power management unit driving five loads, where each load represents a different downstream component. They are (1) resistive, (2) thermal pad heating element, (3) Pulse-width modulated (PWM) resistive, (4) brushless Fan, and (5) LED strip. Using LTSpice, a free circuit simulation software, we simulate each configuration under varying noise levels LTspice (2026) to simulate faulty and healthy conditions across the loads, where a fault is any anomalous condition that causes one or more signals to deviate from their nominal behavior. To ensure training distribution diversity, we vary sample counts across loads (e.g., 5,600 healthy samples for LED strip vs. 2,800 for Thermal pad). Faulty samples comprise approximately 25% of the total dataset, reflecting the class-imbalance typical of real-world deployments. In total, 15 distinct categories including 5 healthy baselines and 10 faulty conditions are introduced (see Appendix, Table 3 ). The simulation experiments produced 12 channels of 116 point time series, including on-state current I ON I_{\text{ON}} , path resistance R PATH R_{\text{PATH}} , and other signals capturing voltage, noise, and spectral properties (see Appendix B and Figure 4 for the simulation details).

blocks.en: 2.2 Reasoning Generation
blocks.zh: 2.2 理性生成

blocks.en:
Next, we generate reasoning traces for each 12-channel time series for all the loads in a multi-stage pipeline: (1) An LLM agent receives fault signatures (e.g., insulation, LED short, connector
degradation), baseline values, hardware specifications via a custom MCP server, and human-authored reasoning
examples for all the faulty and healthy categories. (2) We apply best-of-3 rejection
filtering: generate 3 reasoning candidates and then select the
best (via a separate agent) based on completeness, clarity, and
technical depth. (3) Reasoning traces are structured into
four sections as an expert conducts: signal profile (raw measured value and time series motifs), system
dynamics (physics reasoning), source diagnosis (i.e., fault severity),
and summary (classification and key finding) (4) We prompt the agent to employ Toulmin’s argumentation scheme (i.e., claim, warrant, qualifier, rebuttal Toulmin (1958) ) so that each reasoning trace evaluates candidate fault hypotheses and provides rebuttals to rule out alternatives. (5) Training data embeds inline tool calls (i.e., ohms_law_r (i, v)->$result)) with named variables e.g., $result. Subsequent calls refer to $result to prevent numerical re-typing. During training, tool results are pre-computed and the observation tokens are masked so the model trains on when to call tools and which arguments to pass , rather than memorizing results that the tool returns . At inference, an executor intercepts each call, executes the function, and injects the exact result(s), eliminating cascading arithmetic errors.

blocks.en: 3 Experimental Details
blocks.zh: 3 实验细节

blocks.en: Model Architecture: Our model follows the OpenTSLM soft-prompt architecture Langer et al. (2026) , coupling a time series encoder with a language model through a learned projector. The architecture as presented in Figure 1 has three components: (a) a Transformer-CNN encoder (for brevity, Trans-CNN onwards; 6 layers, 8 heads, d = 128 d{=}128 , patch size 4), (b) a linear projector mapping from 128-dim to the LLM’s 2048-dim, and (c) a frozen Qwen 2.5-3B Yang et al. (2025) with LoRA ( Hu et al., 2022 ) ( r = 16 r{=}16 , α = 32 \alpha{=}32 ) that generates structured reasoning traces from projected sensor tokens. We experiment with two encoder initializations: (a) random (for Trans-CNN), and (b) warm-started from Chronos-T5-tiny Ansari et al. (2025) (see Appendix C ). Each channel is preceded by a text pre-prompt of the form: “Load channel:DC fan, measured mean: 142.3 mA, baseline: 140.0 mA” , providing the model with the channel identity and healthy-condition reference prior to processing the corresponding soft token embeddings. The language model receives the pre-prompts and soft prompt tokens of all channels interleaved in its context window.

(2026),通过学习的投影仪将一个时序编码器与语言模型结合. 图1所示架构有三个组成部分:(a) 变形器-CNN编码器(用于简洁化,横贯CNN;6层,8个头,d=128 d{=}128,补丁尺寸4),(b) 从128-dim到LLM的2048-dim的线性投影仪绘图,(c) 冷冻的Quen 2.5-3B Yang et al. (2025) 与 LoRA (Hu et al., 2022) (r = 16 r{=}16, α = 32\alpha{=}32) 一起,从预测的感应符中产生结构化推理痕迹. 我们试验了两种编码器初始化方法:(a)随机(用于跨CNN)和(b)从Chronos-T5-tiny Ansari等人(2025)开始暖化(见附录C)。 每个频道前都有一个表格的文本预提示: “Load通道:DC风扇,测量平均值:142.3 mA,基线:140.0 mA”,在处理相应的软信使嵌入物之前,为模型提供通道特性和健康条件参考。 语言模型在其上下文窗口中接收所有通道互换的预时速和软提示符.

blocks.en: Model Training: In both architectures, the projector is randomly initialized, so no shared grounding exists between the encoder output space and the language model’s token space. Thus, directly applying supervised fine-tuning under these conditions risks incoherent reasoning. We therefore train through curriculum stages similar to OpenTSLM with some modifications. We inherit OpenTSLM’s Stage 1 (MCQ: multiple choice QA) and Stage 2 (Captioning: description of M4 benchmark time series Makridakis et al. (2020) ). However, neither dataset contains the multivariate electrical signals (e.g., current waveforms, voltage droop, path resistance) that characterize our target domain. Both stages cover financial, weather, and business time series instead. Thus, we introduce a new time series dataset and corresponding simple reasoning structure after Stage 2 and before the final fine-tuning stage. This is our Stage 3 of curriculum training that we introduced, which is based on time series extracted from electrical circuits (the Circuit Time Series (CTS) stage in Figure 1 ). CTS is a large-scale corpus of transient simulations from 1,000 diverse SPICE netlists (i.e., a plain-text description of an electronic circuit with simulations instructions). As mentioned, this stage exposes the model to the breadth of electrical signal behaviors before fine-tuning on the task-specific power management bench data (details in Appendix A and Figure 3 ). Similar to the tool-calling functionality of the SFT stage, we introduced a few simple-tool calls in this stage 3. Finally, in Stage 4, the model is fine-tuned on the Power Management Bench dataset (Section 2.1 ) for fault diagnosis across five load channels and 15 categories including 10 faulty conditions, with class-weighted loss to address the natural imbalance between healthy and fault samples (see Section C.3 for training details). We use a total of 22K training examples, 2.75K validation and test examples, each. Additionally, to test performance beyond the training distribution, we also evaluate on OOD set of 1,050 samples with physically plausible failure modes across the loads (see Tables 3 and 4 in Appendix B )
blocks.zh: 示范培训: 在两种架构中,投影仪都是随机初始化的,因此编码器输出空间和语言模型的符号空间之间不存在共享的地面. 因此,在这些条件下直接实施有监督的微调有可能导致推理不一致。 因此,我们通过类似OpenTSLM的课程阶段进行一些修改。 我们继承了OpenTSLM的第一阶段(MCQ:多选择QA)和第二阶段(Caption:描述M4基准时间序列 Makridakis et al.(2020)). 然而,两个数据集都没有包含作为我们的目标域特征的多变电信号(如电流波形,电压droop,路径阻力). 这两个阶段都涵盖财务、天气和商业时间序列。 因此,我们在第二阶段之后和最后微调阶段之前引入了一个新的时间序列数据集和相应的简单推理结构. 这是我们推出的课程培训第3阶段,它基于从电路中提取的时间序列(图1中的电路时间序列)。 CTS是从1000种不同的SPICE netlists(即对带有模拟指令的电子电路的简单文字描述)的大规模瞬态模拟体. 如前所述,这一阶段在微调特定任务功率管理板凳数据(详见附录A和图3)之前,将模型暴露于电信号行为的广度. 与SFT阶段的工具调用功能类似,我们在此阶段引入了一些简单的工具调用功能. 3个 最后,在第四阶段,该模型在电力管理座椅数据集(第2.1节)上进行了微调,用于在5个载荷通道和15个类别进行断层诊断,包括10个断层条件,同时进行课重损失,以解决健康样品和断层样品之间的自然不平衡(培训详情见C.3节)。 我们总共使用22K训练实例,2.75K验证和测试实例,每个实例. 此外,为了测试培训分配以外的业绩,我们还评估了1 050个装有物理上可行的故障模式的成套OD样本(见附录B表3和表4)。

blocks.en: 4 Rubric-Based Evaluation
blocks.zh: 4 鲁布里克评价

blocks.en: Standard NLP metrics such as ROUGE Lin (2004) and BERTScore Zhang et al. (2020) fail to discriminate between models in constrained technical domains. Since these metrics rely primarily on textual overlap, they suffer from numerical insensitivity and fail to penalize hallucination in numerical generation Janiak et al. (2025) ; Huang et al. (2025) . Likewise, numeric LLM-as-judge scores (“rate from 0 to 1”) are poorly calibrated, brittle and irreproducible. Thus, we repurposed the binary rubric based evaluation as presented in AutoRubric Rao and Callison-Burch (2026) . AutoRubric decomposes evaluation into multiple binary MET/UNMET criteria and demonstrated that binary criteria outperform numeric scores with better correlation with human judgments. We adapt their approach to a physics domain with three additions: (1) code-verified criteria for numerical accuracy that do not require an LLM judge, (2) domain-specific negative scoring for critical failures (wrong diagnosis: − 1 -1 ), and (3) per-load criterion.

blocks.en: We organize evaluation into a total of 22 binary MET/UNMET criteria organized in five categories (see Table 7 for rubric details). Each criterion is either code-verified (JSON parsing, keyword matching, numerical tolerance) or LLM-judged (binary question to a Claude Haiku 5). The rubric is parameterized per load channel to test the tool usage and consistency.

blocks.en: Effect of Reasoning Variants: We compare three reasoning trace variants: (1) direct generative : where the model estimates and calculates numbers in free text (like OpenTSLM Langer et al. (2026) ), (2) equation tags : where the model writes formulas between equation tags but generates the results directly, thus the conclusion can disagree with the formula, and (3) tool calls : where calculations are offloaded to explicit functions and the returned value is chained into later steps, i.e., each number is computed rather than generated and can be verified (see Figure 6 ). While all variants achieve similar 93–94% accuracy, the composite scores reveal a clear hierarchy: 77.98% (direct) vs. 85.85% (equation tags) vs. 94.15% (tool calls). We excluded tool-call related criteria and rescale the scores, so the first two variants are not penalized. However, even then, tool calls produce the most reliable reasoning, because only this variant guarantees correct numerical values and physics calculations.

blocks.en:
Curriculum Learning and Encoder Effects We first evaluate the zero-shot Stage 3 tool-call model, which measures how well the time series understanding learned on CTS transfers to fault diagnosis without Stage 4 supervision. Its composite score of 35.13% shows that it already calls tools and produces structured reasoning while its low accuracy (2.82%) highlights the need for domain alignment, which Stage 4 provides. However, Stage 3 familiarizes the model with electrical signals, and its tool-call reasoning further improves Stage 4 results, particularly benefiting frozen encoder configurations. For Chronos, Stage 3 improves accuracy from 92.70% to 95.42% with a frozen encoder, vs. only 94.64% to 95.10% with a trainable one, suggesting Stage 3 can substitute for encoder fine-tuning. With Stage 3, a frozen Chronos encoder outperforms all Trans-CNN-CTS variants in accuracy and consistency, reaching 95.42% and 97.97% against 94.61% and 97.45% for the better one. This is critical for industrial settings with limited labeled fault data. A frozen, off-the-shelf encoder avoids training from scratch and simplifies domain adaptation by fine-tuning only the projector and the language model. With proper tuning
of the surrounding stages, a frozen Chronos encoder is thus a
practical choice. While per-load performance is omitted for brevity, we observe that thermal pad, fan, and LED strip loads reach very high accuracy (in high 90%) across all model variants, while PWM and resistive loads score between 63-78%, due to the ambiguous boundaries between healthy baseline and early-stage faulty states. Calibrating such domain-specific fault understanding requires further collaboration with the power electronics community.

We also conduct a decoder scaling study across 0.5B, 1.5B, and 3B models

3B models and drops to 83% for the 0.5B model, while consistency drops from 97.5% to 59.3% at 0.5B,

prediction. Notably, the 0.5B tool-call model

confirming that structured reasoning ability contributes more to diagnostic
quality than decoder scale alone. Latency to generate scales from 42 s to

blocks.en:
Reasoning over time series has recently gained significant interest Yang et al. (2026) ; Li et al. (2026) ; Messica et al. (2026) . SensorLM Zhang et al. (2025) aligns sensor and language at scale but produces only statistical captions without physics grounding. Other methods explore anomaly detection Yang et al. (2026) , RL-based knowledge injection He and others (2026) , human-in-the-loop feedback Li and Zhao (2026) , cognitive task taxonomy Qiu et al. (2026) , and symbolic programs Kim et al. (2026) . Closest to our work, OpenTSLM Langer et al. (2026) injects time series
patches into the embedding space of an LLM as soft prompts. Inspired by this design, track differs by: (a) utilizing tool calls to ensure numerical stability, physical correctness, and verifiability by construction and
(b) evaluating with a rubric that assesses reasoning
quality rather than accuracy alone. Time series foundation models such as Chronos Ansari et al. (2024) and
TimesFM Das et al. (2024) , and LLM-based approaches such as
GPT4TS Zhou et al. (2023) and TEMPO Cao et al. (2024) , target forecasting,
whereas track focuses on physics-aware reasoning.

blocks.en: Following Toolformer’s mid-generation token emission Schick et al. (2023) our architecture utilizes physics-specific tool calls. ToolRL Qian et al. (2025) showed RL with decomposed rewards outperforms SFT; we adopt SFT with observation masking and named-variable chaining as pilot RL experiments produced no additional gains. TimeClaw Li and others (2026) employs an agentic runtime; our executor is simpler (10 stateless functions) but guarantees domain-specific correctness. KairosAgent Feng et al. (2026) uses tool calls to form a textual morphology description in the prompt for a pretrained forecasting model whereas track call physics-based tool during generation and applies them to conclude faults with a physics grounding.

blocks.en: Standard LLM judges with numeric scoring Zheng et al. (2023) are often poorly calibrated and irreproducible. AutoRubric Rao and Callison-Burch (2026) achieves stable and interpretable assessments by decomposing evaluation into binary criteria. We adapt this to physics reasoning, checking for physical law application, self-consistency, and causal chain completeness. Appendix F details our rubric.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion and Future Work
blocks.zh: 7 结论和今后的工作

blocks.en: We present track , a tool-augmented time series reasoning architecture for fault diagnosis in multi-load power management systems. By separating reasoning (employing physics law) from computation (executing exact arithmetic via tools), a 3B-parameter model achieves reliable diagnostics across 15 categories on five load channel. Our rubric-based evaluation provides actionable per-criterion feedback to guide targeted model improvement, a capability absent from standard NLP metrics. We compare different variants and observe off-the-shelf encoders (e.g., Chronos) seem a practical choice for real world deployments. Future work includes RL with tool-specific rewards Qian et al. (2025) , rubric-driven prompt optimization, and reducing latency in real-time implementation.
blocks.zh: 我们在多负荷电源管理系统中呈现一个故障诊断工具化的时间序列推理架构。 通过将推理(运用物理定律)与计算(通过工具执行精确算术)分开,3B参数模型在五个负载通道上实现15个类别的可靠诊断. 我们基于主题的评价提供了可操作的每个标准反馈,以指导目标模型的改进,这是标准NLP衡量标准中缺少的能力。 我们比较不同的变体,观察现成的编码器(如Chronos),似乎是现实世界部署的实际选择. 今后的工作包括具有特定工具奖励的RL Qian等人。 (2025),rumric驱动的即时优化,减少实时执行中的延迟.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: We have used a few generative tools for slight paraphrasing and grammar check in the text. SLM is used here to generate reasoning traces and certainly they have standard limitations such as non-deterministic nature of generation. We use large SOTA agents as LLM-as-a-judge, although, our binary rubric method is more effective, they can be brittle sometimes and hard to reproduce the exact accuracy values. Finally, although we have implemented our model running on a Jetson Orin module we plan to improve the compute efficiency and reduce the latency in the future.

blocks.en: 8 Ethical Statement
blocks.zh: 8 道德声明

blocks.en: We do not foresee any potential negative societal impacts of our work. However, our reasoning model(s) are built upon LLMs, which are non-deterministic in nature. In reality, since our work is applied to Physical AI, extreme care must be taken before directly implementing LLM-generated outputs in real world environments.
blocks.zh: 我们预计我们的工作不会产生任何潜在的负面社会影响。 然而,我们的推理模式建立在LLMs之上,后者的性质是非决定性的。 在现实中,由于我们的工作被应用于物理AI,在现实世界环境中直接实施LLM产生的产出之前,必须极其谨慎.

blocks.en: Appendix A Circuit Time Series (CTS)
blocks.zh: 附录A 电路时间系列

blocks.en: This dataset is built by running transient simulations on a collection of 1,000 open-source SPICE netlists Said et al. (2023) 1 1 1 https://github.com/symbench/spice-datasets . Each simulation produces a time series of node voltages (junctions in a circuit) and branch currents sampled at various sampling rate ranging between 10 10 and 100 100 kHz. We select these netlists such that they span a wide range of circuit types such as power regulators, oscillators, filters, and mixed-signal ICs. We only consider netlists with fewer than 15 nodes, which keeps the number of observed time series reasonable (i.e., fewer than 30). We also vary the settling time across circuits, so that the dataset covers the full range of transient behaviors.
blocks.zh: 这个数据集是通过在1000个开源的SPICE网列表上运行瞬态模拟来构建的 Said等人(2023年),11 1 https://github.com/symbench/spice-datasets. 每一次模拟产生一个时间序列的节点电压(电路中的节点)和分支电流以10-100千赫的不同采样速率取样. 我们选择这些网路列表,这样它们可以跨越广泛的电路类型,如电源调节器,振荡器,滤波器,以及混合信号的IC. 我们只考虑少于15个节点的网状列表,这样可以使观测到的时间序列数量合理(即少于30个). 我们还改变整个电路的安放时间, 以便数据集涵盖全部瞬间行为。

blocks.en: We then pair each time series with a structured annotation that contains explicit reasoning traces in the form of physics tool calls. For example, at a given node the annotation applies Kirchhoff’s current law, which trains the model to verify the law rather than only describe the waveform. To the best of our knowledge, Circuit Time Series is the first large-scale time series corpus derived from circuit netlists and paired with a reasoning corpus (see Figure 3 for an example).
blocks.zh: 然后我们把每个时序配上一个结构化的注释,其中包含物理工具调用形式的明确推理痕迹. 例如,在给定的节点上,注释应用了Kirchhoff的现行法律,即训练模型以验证法律,而不是仅仅描述波形。 据我们所知,电路时间系列是第一个从电路网列表中衍生出来,并配以推理器的大型时间序列体(例见图3).

blocks.en: We create a simulation of a power management system that drives five different loads. Similar to the Circuit Time Series dataset, we run the simulation in transient analysis and record raw voltage and current waveforms at 3.2kHz. We then process these raw waveforms with a sliding window (5 s windows, 1 s step, 120 s recordings) to extract one scalar parameter per window per channel. Each window is characterized by 12 physical parameters, including on-state current I ON I_{\text{ON}} , leakage current I OFF I_{\text{OFF}} , path resistance R PATH R_{\text{PATH}} , and nine others capturing voltage, noise, and spectral properties. Figure 6 shows the three reasoning-trace variants in detail for the same
time-series sample, with each section annotated. In signal_profile , the model
reports numerical statistics (e.g., mean and standard deviation) of the relevant features.
In system_dynamics , it evaluates the individual system properties from the

blocks.en: To test model performance beyond the training distribution, we additionally construct an explicit out-of-distribution (OOD) set of 1050 samples with physically plausible failure modes intentionally selected to differ from the training fault conditions. Each OOD condition is mapped to its nearest ID label, the fault whose circuit behavior is most similar in terms of load characteristics and affected channel. The key challenge is that while the load and fault label are the same, the time series signatures differ: for example, a wrong-value resistor on the resistive load shares the same channel as a resistive short but produces a different current profile. The model is therefore expected to reason over the deviation pattern rather than recognize a memorized signature, correctly assigning the nearest label while identifying the true underlying anomaly.
blocks.zh: 为了测试在培训分配之外的模式性能,我们另外建造了一套明确的分配外样本(OO),其中1050个样本具有物理上可行的故障模式,有意选择与培训故障条件不同的模式。 每个OOD条件都被映射到其最近的ID标签上,这个断层的电路行为在负载特性和受影响的通道上最相似. 关键的挑战在于,虽然负载和故障标签相同,但时间序列的签名有所不同:例如,在阻负载上一个错误的值阻抗器与阻抗短器共用同一个通道,但产生不同的当前剖面. 因此,预计该模型会对偏差模式作出解释,而不是识别一个记着的签名,正确指定最近的标签,同时查明真正的反常情况。

blocks.en: Appendix C Model Architecture Details
blocks.zh: 附录C 模型结构细节

blocks.en: C.1 Transformer CNN:
blocks.zh: C.1 变形器CNN:

blocks.en: We employ a encoder module (called Trans-CNN encoder). It splits the input time series into non-overlapping patches via a strided convolution and projects each patch into a fixed-dimensional embedding. We add learnable positional embeddings to encode patch position, apply layer normalisation and dropout, and pass the result to a stack of transformer encoder layers with multi-head self-attention and GELU feed-forward sublayers. Each channel is encoded independently, so the self-attention captures temporal structure within a single channel only. Cross-channel reasoning is delegated to the language model, which receives the soft prompt tokens of all channels interleaved with their text descriptions in its context window.
blocks.zh: 我们使用一个编码器模块(称为跨CNN编码器). 它将输入时间序列通过串联分解为非重叠补丁,并将每个补丁投影为固定维嵌入. 我们在编码补丁位置上添加可学习的定位嵌入,应用层常态化和退出,并将结果传递给一叠具有多头自留心和GELU饲料前置子层的变压器编码器层. 每个信道都是独立编码的,所以自觉只在一个信道内捕捉时间结构. 跨通道推理被委托给语言模型,语言模型接收所有通道与其上下文窗口中的文字描述交互的软提示.

blocks.en: C.3 Training Setup.
blocks.zh: C.3 培训设置。

blocks.en:
All models are trained on H100 GPUs using standard hyperparameters: AdamW
optimizer, bf16 precision, effective batch size of 16, and early stopping
with a patience of 5. Stages 1-3 are shared across configurations; St4
experiments branch from the same Stage 3 checkpoint, ensuring that
differences in final performance are attributable solely to St4 design
choices. For example, the frozen and trainable encoder variants of
Trans-CNN-CTS both initialize from the identical St3 checkpoint and
diverge only in whether the encoder weights receive gradients during St4
fine-tuning in the frozen variant only the projector and decoder are
updated, while in the trainable variant the full model is end-to-end
optimised.

We implement the system for real-time testing on a power management bench. Our
setup has three components: (i) a power management bench that drives five loads
(resistive, thermal pad, PWM-controlled, fan, and an LED driver), (ii) a
microcontroller board that samples the input voltage (VIN) and input current
(IIN) of these loads at 3.2 kHz and extracts parameters from the samples, and
(iii) a Jetson Orin module that runs the reasoning model for fault diagnosis.

blocks.en:
We present the rubric in Table 7 that has been used to compute the composite score in Table 2 and Table 6 . On the one hand, most of the criteria are checked by code. For example, we verify that the output have a valid JSON with all four sections, and it must stay within the word budget. The signal profile must report the measured values without interpretation and match the
ground-truth statistics. The physics reasoning must verify Ohm’s law with approved tool calls
and ground its numbers in the prompt baseline with accurate equations. The diagnosis must match
the gold fault label, and the summary must contain a diagnosis, a confidence level, and an
action. On the other hand, an LLM judge covers the criteria that need semantic judgment (i.e. cross-parameter
reasoning, root-cause explanation, the causal chain from fault to signature, the rebuttal of
alternative faults). We also evalute whether the conclusion follows the reasoning (reports as consistency metric). Some of the critical checks have also a penalty when they fail.
